heading: 8.8 Forms over two values of one type
text:
### 8.8 Forms over two values of one type [LUNI.8.8]

The operands of the two-argument `min` and `max` ([LEXP.3.8.1]), of `??`
([LNUL.5.3]) and of `..` ([LINT.2.2]), the point and the interval of `in`
([LINT.3.1.3]), and two intervals that a relation or an equality compares
([LINT.3.2.2], [LINT.4.2], [LINT.5.4]) stand beside each other as the operands of
`+` do. The compiler **must** refuse a bare number beside a dimensioned value
([LUNI.8.3]), a `Duration` included ([LTIM.1.3.5]), and two values of different
dimensions ([LUNI.8.2]), with `DS_VALIDATE_DIM_MISMATCH`.

Values of one dimension are valid, and the result has that dimension. An interval
of them carries it, and a point or another interval is checked against it. An
operand whose type the compiler cannot determine is not refused here
([LUNI.8.3]).
